decisions.reason: The prohibited term and product-benefit clarification affect script messaging, but do not change the current reference-led creative basis or its relationship to the reference.
The source does not change the target age range, Indian-market context, or any other audience attribute.
The messaging clarification does not change the source or presentation of testimonial material.
The source neither changes nor removes the requirement for a naturally integrated call to action.
Prohibiting one Hindi term constrains product messaging but does not change the requirement that the script and preview be in Hindi.
The source does not change the required directness or Indian-market suitability of the opening hook.
The term prohibition and benefit alignment do not alter the independently required viral creative style.
The source concerns script wording and product claims, not lip-sync accuracy or facial-expression performance.
The source does not resolve or otherwise change the production-method conflict concerning live-action and AI-generated visuals.
The messaging decision does not change responsibility for the script, visuals, voiceover, or client-supplied inputs.
The source does not change actor nationality or gender preferences.
The source does not change video counts, duration, aspect ratios, or the pilot and follow-on ordering conditions.
